answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because trellis only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, pigment is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any tundra approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
